title: Greeting to Polycarp, bishop of Smyrna
english: Ignatius, who is also called God-Bearer, sends very many greetings to Polycarp, bishop of the church of Smyrna, or rather to one who is watched over by God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
orientation: Ignatius opens his letter to Polycarp, bishop of the church in Smyrna, with a formal greeting.

title: Exhortation to Polycarp as bishop
english: I welcome your purpose in God, fixed as on an immovable rock, and I glorify Him exceedingly, because I have been deemed worthy of your blameless face. May I have benefit from it in God.

I urge you, by the grace with which you have been clothed, to press on in your course and to urge everyone, so that they may be saved. Defend your place with all care, both fleshly and spiritual. Care for unity, than which nothing is better. Bear everyone, as the Lord also bears you. Endure everyone in love, just as you are already doing.

Devote yourself to unceasing prayers. Ask for understanding greater than what you have. Keep watch, possessing a sleepless spirit. Speak to each person according to the manner of God. Bear the illnesses of everyone as a perfect athlete. Where there is more labor, there is much gain.
orientation: Ignatius is writing to Polycarp, bishop of Smyrna, and has just greeted him; now he begins his direct exhortation to him as a bishop.

title: Advice to Polycarp on shepherding and self-discipline
english: If you love good disciples, that earns you no credit. Rather, bring the more troublesome into subjection with gentleness. Not every wound is healed by the same remedy. Stop inflammations with soothing compresses.

Be wise as the serpent and pure as the dove (Matthew 10:16). For this reason you are both fleshly and spiritual, so that you may deal gently with the things that appear before your face; but ask that the invisible things may be revealed to you, so that you may lack nothing and abound in every gift.

The time demands you, as pilots deal with winds and as a storm-tossed man needs a harbor, to attain God. Be sober, as God's athlete. The prize is incorruption and eternal life, about which you also are persuaded. In every respect I am your ransom, and my bonds too, which you loved.
orientation: Ignatius is writing to Polycarp, bishop of Smyrna, giving him direct instructions on how to lead his church and prepare himself for martyrdom.

title: Stand firm as an anvil under the blows
english: Do not let those who seem trustworthy but teach falsely terrify you. Stand firm as an anvil being struck. It is the mark of a great athlete to be beaten and to win. Above all, for God's sake we must endure everything, so that he also may endure us.

Become more eager than you already are. Discern the seasons. I await the one who is beyond time, the timeless one, the invisible one, who for our sake became visible, the one beyond suffering, who for our sake became subject to suffering, who endured in every way for us.
orientation: Ignatius is addressing Polycarp, bishop of Smyrna, urging him to remain steadfast amid false teachers and to endure all things for God's sake.

title: Care for widows, slaves, and the church's gatherings
english: Do not neglect the widows. After the Lord, you yourself must be their caretaker. Let nothing happen without your judgment, and do nothing yourself without God. Indeed, you do not do so. Be steadfast.
Let the church meetings take place more frequently. Seek out everyone by name.

Do not despise slaves, whether men or women. But they too must not become conceited. Instead, let them serve all the more for the glory of God, so that they may obtain a better freedom from God. They must not long to be freed at the church's expense, lest they be found slaves of desire.
orientation: Ignatius is giving direct instructions to Polycarp, bishop of Smyrna, about how to order the church's life.

title: Marriage, Purity, and the Bishop's Approval
english: Flee from evil arts, and rather speak about these things. Speak kindly to my sisters, telling them to love the Lord and to be content with their husbands in flesh and spirit. Likewise command my brothers in the name of Jesus Christ to love their wives as the Lord loves the church.

If anyone is able to remain in continence for the honor of the Lord's flesh, let him remain without boasting. If he boasts, he has perished; and if he is esteemed more highly than the bishop, he has been corrupted. It is fitting for men and women who marry to make their union with the bishop's judgment, so that the marriage may be according to the Lord and not according to desire. Let all things be done for the honor of God.
orientation: Ignatius is giving instructions to Polycarp, bishop of Smyrna, about how to teach the brothers and sisters in his church regarding marriage and purity.

title: Soldiers of God: heed the bishop and keep your equipment
english: Pay close attention to the bishop, so that God may pay close attention to you. I offer my very life for those who submit to the bishop, the council of elders, and the deacons. May I be counted worthy to have a share with them in God. Labor together, struggle together, run together, suffer together, rest together, and rise together as God's stewards, counselors, and servants.

Please the one in whose army you serve, the one from whom you also receive your wages. Let none of you be found a deserter. Let your baptism remain as your armor, your faith as a helmet, your love as a spear, your endurance as full battle gear. Your works are your deposits, so that you may receive back what is due to you. Be patient with one another, then, in gentleness, as God is with you. May I have joy in you always.
orientation: Ignatius is writing to the church in Smyrna, urging them to unite under their bishop, elders, and deacons, and now gives them a series of military-style exhortations about shared labor and spiritual armor.

title: Send a runner to Syria to glorify God
english: Since the church in Antioch of Syria is at peace, as I have been told, because of your prayer, I too have become more cheerful, free from care in God, if only through suffering I may attain God, so that I may be found in the resurrection as your disciple.

It is fitting, Polycarp, most blessed by God, to convene a gathering most befitting God and to ordain someone whom you hold very dear and who is untiring, one who can be called a courier for God. Deem this man worthy to go to Syria and glorify your untiring love for the glory of God.

A Christian has no authority over himself, but is devoted to God. This is God's work and yours, when you complete it. For I trust in grace, that you are ready for good-doing belonging to God. Knowing your intensity for the truth, I have encouraged you with few words.
orientation: Ignatius, writing to Polycarp of Smyrna, has just learned that the church in Antioch is at peace and now asks Polycarp to convene a council and appoint a messenger to Syria.

title: Final instructions and greetings to Polycarp
english: I could not write to all the churches, because I had to sail suddenly from Troas to Neapolis, as God's will commands. So you should write to the churches ahead, since you have acquired God's purpose, so that they too may do the same: those who are able can send men on foot, and others can send letters through the men you send. In this way you may be glorified by an eternal work, as one who is worthy.

I greet everyone by name, and Epitrope with her whole household and her children. I greet Attalus, my beloved. I greet the one who is to be deemed worthy to go to Syria. Grace will be with him always, and with Polycarp who sends him.
I pray that you may be strong always in our God Jesus Christ, in whom may you remain in the unity of God and under the bishop. I greet Alce, the name dear to me. Be strong in the Lord.
orientation: Ignatius is closing his letter to Polycarp, bishop of Smyrna, asking him to send messengers or letters to the churches ahead and sending final greetings.
